Below are concise answers and next steps. I also attached a draft "reranker_test_plan.xlsx" and a small sample CSV in the Drive link Soojin referenced.

Answers:
- Auth & SDKs: Redwood SDK accepts bearer tokens. For Dedicated we integrate with customer-managed auth in two ways: (a) JWT passthrough — your gateway issues JWTs and our gateway validates them against your JWKS; or (b) short-lived Redwood API tokens minted via an OIDC exchange. For an evaluation, JWT passthrough is simplest and avoids static keys. We’ll provide a JWT example and SDK config snippet.

- Routing & latency: Yes — Dedicated can be pinned to your VPC region and routed locally (no egress across regions) if you run Redwood Private or Dedicated in that region. For Hosted, routing may vary. Regarding batching: for ~50 candidates we recommend a single rerank call where you send the candidate text vectors and metadata in one request; Redwood’s continuous-batching will optimize throughput. If you need strict P95 < 100ms, split into parallel sub-requests + then merge, but that increases token/compute cost.

- Scoring semantics: the reranker API returns a normalized relevance score in [0,1] (post-softmax ranking score) and a raw score field for diagnostics. You can threshold on normalized_score for business rules.

- Default metrics: our evaluation report includes Precision@k (P@1,P@5), NDCG@10, MRR, and a custom pairwise WinRate if you provide binary preference labels. We’ll export CSV-ready metrics plus a small HTML report.

- Data handling: On Dedicated our control plane still coordinates deployments, but inference traffic (token-level inputs and vector payloads) can be kept inside your VPC via a dedicated egress path — no token payloads leave your VPC for inference. We’ll run a short security checklist and sign the infra diagram for your Security team.

Proposed test plan highlights (from attachment):
- Input: sample_eval_queries.csv (100–500 labeled queries) + candidate pools (top 100 retrieval candidates per query)
- Runs: baseline (your current ranker), Redwood reranker (default top_k=10), Redwood tuned (top_k sweep: 5/10/20 + re-ranking thresholding)
- Metrics: P@1,P@5,NDCG@10,MRR,latency P50/P95, cost-per-query estimate
- Deliverables: metric CSV, HTML visual report, recommended top_k and threshold for production

Quick notes on top_k tuning:
- For reranker models, increasing top_k beyond 20 usually gives diminishing returns for short queries; we suggest trying 5/10/20 on your sample and plotting delta NDCG vs compute.
- If you want to enforce strict tail latency, set top_k lower and use prefix/KV caching for repeated queries.
